title: fix(superheroes): stack merges work in a cloud session, through REST merge-async
body:
Closes #2103.

Closes #2098 (layer 2 of 2, based on layer 1's branch, the PR for #2102 — #2104).

## What's changing, and why

In a cloud session `gh stack merge` cannot run, because GitHub's proxy refuses GraphQL, so a cloud merge train could not merge any stack. A new helper, `lib/stack_merge.py`, merges a stack through GitHub's REST `merge-async` endpoint instead. It asks GitHub to squash-merge the stack's top pull request, which merges everything up to and including it, pinned to the head the membership re-read saw, and waits for GitHub's answer. It says "merged", and exits 0, only when GitHub reports the merge done and the merged head is the pinned one. A merge GitHub queued, refused or failed, a head that moved, a request that is still pending when its time runs out, and any answer it cannot read all come back as "not merged" with a reason. A pending merge also returns the id that resumes the wait. The doctrine (`rubric/native-stacks.md`, the merge train) names the helper as the cloud equivalent of `gh stack merge`. Local merges are unchanged.

## What we're accepting

- **The merge request is not live-tested against GitHub.** A live call would merge a real stack on your repository. The request and response shapes come from GitHub's REST documentation. Only the "unknown request" 404 was recorded from the real API. The first real cloud stack merge is the helper's first live run; if GitHub's answers differ from the documentation, it reports "not merged" (it never reads an unexpected answer as merged).
- **A queued merge is reported "not merged".** When the base branch has a merge queue, GitHub queues the stack and the helper returns `merge-enqueued`; the train reads the stack back later, as for `gh stack merge`.
- **Two minor findings read "waiting for you" in the review record.** One is real and left on purpose (next bullet). The other, the read-back's time budget, was fixed in `8ec2f438` and cleared by the last audit; the record could not tie the fix to it. Confirming it fixed is all it needs.
- **One minor test-realism finding is left for you** (see the review dispositions): the timing tests use a fake clock that cannot show the clock crossing the deadline between two reads inside one loop step. The path it would hide ends in the same clean "timed out" result, because a negative subprocess timeout raises the timeout error the loop already catches (checked by running it). Fixing it would be a third rework of the same poll loop, which the build rules stop at.
- **One review step was decided by the builder, not by you.** The review routed "the default wait outlives the 600-second tool limit" to an owner-judgment gate. No owner was present, and the launch lets the builder take design calls inside the issue's scope with disclosure. The builder chose "fix it": one 420-second budget for the whole merge. The review journal records that call as `owner-unattributed`.
- The PR-body grounding seat did not run, because the auto-fix review loop has no phase for it.

## How to see it

N/A — say it: a library and doctrine change with no running app. The evidence is the tests and the review below.

## Advisor vet
<!-- superheroes:advisor-vet -->

**Verdict: READY** · 8ec2f4383dd34386062c3879d5f8ea1068e6f9c0 as a layer (held with the stack: it merges only together with #2104)

**What was checked.** I checked the merge helper against GitHub's own documentation: it asks GitHub to merge the whole stack, pinned to the exact version that was reviewed, and it says "merged" only when GitHub says "merged". I walked every other answer (refused, queued, failed, still waiting, unreadable, a different version) and none reads as merged. I broke the newest safety checks on purpose and the tests caught each one, which also proves the "time budget" finding the review left open is really fixed.

The review left two small findings for you; both are cards on the stack's sheet.

**What accepting it means.**
- The first real cloud stack merge will be this helper's first live run against GitHub. If GitHub answers differently from its documentation, the helper says "not merged"; it never claims a merge that did not happen.
- "Not merged" does not always mean nothing merged. If another merge request was already running, or GitHub's answer was malformed, GitHub may still finish the merge. Read the stack back before trying again.
- A queued merge (a repository with a merge queue) is reported "not merged" and may land in parts.
- After this lands, the launcher's dependency check and the wave watch's repository read still fail in a cloud session (proposed separately).

**What is yours to decide.**
1. Accept that the first real cloud stack merge is the helper's first live test.
2. Ratify the builder's call, made without you: one 420-second wait limit for the whole merge, so a "still waiting" answer and its resume id always print before the host's 10-minute cut-off.
3. Accept the one test-timing leftover (it can only end as "timed out, not merged") and confirm the read-back time-limit finding as fixed.

Receipt: see the vet 624 comment on this PR.

Head `8ec2f4383dd34386062c3879d5f8ea1068e6f9c0`. This layer holds the merge-async 404 fixture, WO-B, WO-C's merge hunks (unchanged from the integrated branch), and the review fixes WO-D, WO-E and the review loop's fixer commits `9cb9511a`, `579bf467` and `8ec2f438`.

The path ends in `poll-timeout` because a negative subprocess timeout raises `TimeoutExpired`, which the loop catches (checked: `subprocess.run(..., timeout=-0.5)` raises `TimeoutExpired`). A fix would be a third rework of the poll loop (WO-D, WO-E), which the tripwire stops |

S3's terminal: `converged`, certification `audited-chain` (a scoped certifying finish over the fix audits and scoped finders, not a fresh full panel), independence `independent`. Review record: https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/pull/2105#issuecomment-6375762004 — status **`not-reviewed`**, because two findings read "waits for the owner's decision": (1) the fake-clock Minor, a disclosed leftover; and (2) "give the head read-back only the remaining invocation budget", which **was fixed** in `8ec2f438`. Round 3's audit ruled its parent finding `discharged`: "The prior audit's deadline-extension objection is resolved: `left = start + poll_timeout - monotonic()` supplies only" the time left. The disposition ledger did not mark the audit-spawned finding fixed under its own key. Both need the owner's or the advisor's word on the sheet. Raw outputs: [S1](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/pull/2105#issuecomment-6374733300), [S2](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/pull/2105#issuecomment-6375074977), [S3](https://github.com/zwrose/superheroes/pull/2105#issuecomment-6375479227).

### Bite-proof records

`plugins/superheroes/lib/tests/bite_proofs/wo_stack_merge_2098.md`: WO-B's 28 guards, WO-D's P6 and WO-E's P7. **Re-run by me** in a detached probe worktree, with Edit-tool neutralizations restored by the inverse edit, using `scripts/pinned-python -B -X pycache_prefix=/tmp/superheroes-pyc-bp -m pytest plugins/superheroes/lib/tests/test_stack_merge.py -q -p no:cacheprovider -k <expr>`:

The first S1 attempt ran before the edit had applied (the file had not been read), so it showed `19 passed`. I record it as the un-neutralized baseline, and the red above came from the applied edit. The probe tree was clean after each restore. The review fixer's guards (the head read-back in `579bf467` and its budget in `8ec2f438`) carry tests the round-2 and round-3 audits read; I did not re-run them as bite-proofs.
